problem: Real-world navigation datasets for imitation learning are small, or (YouTube-mined) lack metric trajectories and range sensing. Existing datasets also treat navigation and scene semantics (language goals, traversability) as separate tasks.
motivation: Data-driven visual, vision-language and semantics-aware navigation needs large, diverse, real-world data with metric odometry. A human-worn egocentric rig with a stereo camera can collect such data cheaply, and automatic foundation-model pipelines can add semantic annotations.
key_idea: Release EgoWalk, a 50-hour egocentric human walking dataset with RGB-D and odometry, plus automatically generated language-goal annotations and traversability masks, and show its use for fine-tuning navigation policies.
insight: Fine-tuning existing visual navigation foundation models on human egocentric walking data gives large real-robot gains despite the embodiment gap (ViNT 0.44 to 0.89, NoMaD 0.10 to 0.33). The language pipelines show that the end-to-end VLM approach selects goals more reliably (99.6% vs 92.3%) while Goal-Boxes gives tighter metric grounding. Pose estimation on EgoWalk is much harder than on the standard benchmarks for DA3, so the data exposes room for improvement.
method: Data collection: chest-mounted ZED 2 stereo camera plus Jetson ZED Box in a backpack; recorded at 30 FPS, then depth and visual-inertial odometry extracted offline and downsampled to 5 FPS; faces blurred with OWL-ViT; guidelines for robot-centric, social, collision-avoidance and turn-heavy trajectories.

Goal-Boxes language pipeline: RAM + Grounding DINO detect candidate objects, which are back-projected with depth and filtered by tag blacklist, box size and distance; the object closest to the future odometry trajectory is chosen, and Gemini 3 Flash captions the crop (brief and detailed, with synonyms). Yields 50,019 captions.

End-to-End language pipeline: 11-second chunks sampled at 1 FPS are given to Gemini 3 Flash, which picks goals, writes captions and reports the frame where the object leaves view. Yields 31,504 captions.

Traversability masks: future odometry is projected onto the image as footsteps using the known camera height, and used as SAM prompts; both the top-score and the largest-area masks are stored (more than 30k samples).
Policy fine-tuning: ViNT and NoMaD are fine-tuned from official checkpoints on EgoWalk only and deployed on an AgileX Tracer robot with an RGB-only Azure Kinect.

Auxiliary demos: distilling SAM masks into lightweight segmentation networks, and a Depth Anything 3 reconstruction, pose-estimation and Gaussian splatting demo with a 60-subtrajectory pose benchmark.

setting.backbone: ViNT and NoMaD (fine-tuned from official checkpoints); segmentation nets (Segformer, U-Net, DeepLabV3+, FPN, U-Net++); Gemini 3 Flash (frozen) for annotation
setting.model_size: segmentation models 6M-26M params; ViNT/NoMaD sizes not stated
setting.training_data: EgoWalk: 50 hours of human egocentric walking in Moscow (5 FPS, RGB-D + odometry) as the sole fine-tuning data; the 30k-sample traversability set for segmentation
setting.observation: monocular RGB from an Azure Kinect on the robot (dataset: ZED stereo RGB-D + odometry)
setting.action_space: waypoint prediction from ViNT/NoMaD, followed by a topological-graph controller
setting.privileged: none at test time; a pre-recorded topological graph of the environment (recorded about 24 hours earlier) is used for goal-image navigation

numbers.eval_set_note: 3 indoor environments x 3 trials = 9 runs, all unseen

numbers_note: No standard VLN/ObjectNav benchmark. Language annotation quality is in Table lang_eval: Goal Selection Acc. 92.3 (Goal-Boxes, 738 samples) vs 99.6 (End-to-End, 747 samples); Caption Quality 89.3 vs 99.2.
results: Fine-tuning on EgoWalk raises real-robot success from 0.44 to 0.89 for ViNT and from 0.10 to 0.33 for NoMaD in unseen indoor environments. Lightweight segmentation nets reach IoU up to 0.9265, and the End-to-End language pipeline is 99.1% all-good vs 87.7% for Goal-Boxes.
limitations: Human trajectories are noisy and may contain near-collisions or maneuvers infeasible for robots; the ZED VIO odometry can fail in low light.
Annotation pipelines are heuristic and can be wrong in edge cases; traversability masks have no formal quality evaluation.
Real-robot evaluation is small (9 runs per model, indoor only) and shows no controlled comparison against other datasets.
builds_on: Kim et al. traversability learning from footsteps
